group.passage: Until 1895, doctors could judge what was going on inside a living body only from the outside. The timeline below traces seven milestones in medical imaging: who made each one, what it revealed and where it fell short.

passage_parts.title: Wilhelm Röntgen
passage_parts.text: While testing a glass tube in Germany, Röntgen noticed invisible rays that passed easily through flesh but far less easily through bone. His picture of his wife’s hand, showing her bones and wedding ring, astonished the public, and within months doctors were using the rays to locate broken bones and bullets.

passage_parts.title: Thomas Edison
passage_parts.text: Edison built a viewer with a glowing screen, and crowds lined up to see their own bones. His assistant, Clarence Dally, spent hours holding his hands in front of the tubes. Like many researchers of the day, he assumed his burns would heal with rest, but he lost both arms and died in 1904. Shocked, Edison gave up X-ray work.

passage_parts.title: Ian Donald
passage_parts.text: Working with an engineer, this Glasgow doctor adapted a machine that factories used to find cracks in metal. It sent ultrasound, sound too high for human ears, into the body and turned the echoes into pictures, and his 1958 report with colleagues included the first such images of a baby in the womb. Bone and air, however, block the sound.

passage_parts.title: Godfrey Hounsfield
passage_parts.text: Ordinary X-ray photographs showed bones sharply but left the brain looking like fog. Hounsfield’s scanner sent beams through the head from many angles while a computer turned the readings into thin slices, and in its first patient it revealed a brain tumor. CT has proved a double-edged sword, though: because it relies on X-rays, too many scans can be harmful.

passage_parts.label: Mid-1970s
passage_parts.title: A team in St. Louis
passage_parts.text: Before a PET scan, patients receive a form of sugar that carries a tiny amount of radioactive material. Cancer cells use sugar faster than healthy ones, so they light up on the screen. PET therefore shows how tissue is working rather than what it looks like.

passage_parts.title: Raymond Damadian
passage_parts.text: Using a huge magnet and radio waves instead of X-rays, his team made the first MRI image of a human body, a rough picture of a chest that took nearly five hours to produce. Today’s machines are far quicker and show soft tissue in fine detail, but patients must lie perfectly still, since any movement turns the picture into a blur.

passage_parts.title: Seiji Ogawa
passage_parts.text: Ogawa, a researcher in the United States, found that MRI could detect how much oxygen the blood was carrying. Because busy brain areas draw in extra oxygen-rich blood, scientists could watch the brain at work while a volunteer looked at flashing lights or moved a hand.

questions.stem:
From (A) to (H) below, choose the statements that can be inferred from the timeline.
請選出正確的選項，並劃記在答題卷作答區內。（多選題，4分）

options.A: Early X-ray workers did not realize how dangerous the rays were.
options.B: Ultrasound was first designed for looking at unborn babies.
options.C: Moving a hand can send extra blood to parts of the brain.
options.D: CT scans expose patients to no radiation at all.
options.E: PET shows tissue at work rather than its shape.
options.F: PET avoids radiation by using sugar instead of rays.
options.G: Ogawa’s method was the first to show a living brain.
options.H: Edison quit X-ray work because his viewer showed nothing useful.

questions.stem: Which noun phrase in the timeline describes “something that brings both benefits and risks”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: 1971 年的條目說 CT 是一把雙面刃：因為它仰賴 X 光，掃描太多次可能「有害」（too many scans can be harmful）；1896 年的條目也說，愛迪生的助手 Dally 以為手上的灼傷休息就會好，結果失去雙臂、在 1904 年過世，可見早期的先驅並不知道射線會造成多大的傷害。摘要句 had no idea how much ___ the rays could do to their own bodies 中，how much 後面要接不可數名詞，而且要能和動詞 do 搭配：do harm (to sb.) 是固定用法，意為「對（某人）造成傷害」。把形容詞 harmful 改成名詞 harm。
evidence: CT has proved a double-edged sword, though: because it relies on X-rays, too many scans can be harmful.
Like many researchers of the day, he assumed his burns would heal with rest, but he lost both arms and died in 1904.
1.strategy_zh: how much ___ the rays could do：空格是 do 的受詞，前面有 how much，要填不可數名詞。上下文說先驅們付出了健康的代價，所以要找文中表示「傷害」的字。1971 年的條目用形容詞 harmful 說明掃描太多次的後果，把它改回名詞 harm（do harm＝造成傷害）。
hints: how much ___：要填不可數名詞，而且能和動詞 do 搭配（do ___ to someone）。
哪一個條目用一個形容詞說明 X 光掃描做太多次的後果？
把形容詞 harmful 改成名詞。

2.explanation_zh: 1977 年的條目說，今天的 MRI 雖然快得多、能把軟組織呈現得很細緻，但病人必須完全靜止地躺著，因為任何移動都會讓影像「變成一片模糊」（turns the picture into a blur）。摘要句 its images can be ___ by the slightest motion 是被動語態（can be＋過去分詞，by 帶出造成的原因），要填過去分詞；把名詞 blur 當動詞用（blur 也可作動詞「使模糊」），改成過去分詞 blurred（字尾 r 要重複），意為「被弄得模糊」。
evidence: Today’s machines are far quicker and show soft tissue in fine detail, but patients must lie perfectly still, since any movement turns the picture into a blur.
2.strategy_zh: can be ___ by the slightest motion：被動語態，要填過去分詞。摘要句說 MRI 雖然不用 X 光，仍有自己的弱點，回到 1977 年的條目找「移動」會對影像造成什麼結果，把那個名詞當動詞用，再改成過去分詞。
hints: can be ___ by…：被動語態，要填過去分詞。
1977 年的條目說病人為什麼必須完全靜止？任何移動會把影像變成什麼？
把名詞 blur 當動詞用，改成過去分詞（注意字尾子音要重複）。

3.explanation_zh: 題目要選「可以從時間軸推論出來」的敘述。(A) 1896 年的條目說，愛迪生的助手 Dally 一連好幾個小時把雙手放在射線管前，而且「和當時許多研究者一樣」以為灼傷休息就會好，結果失去雙臂並過世，愛迪生大受震驚而放棄 X 光研究；可推知早期使用 X 光的人並不知道射線有多危險。(C) 1990 年的條目說，正在活動的腦區會引進更多富含氧氣的血液，所以科學家能在受試者看閃爍的燈光或動手時觀察大腦運作；可推知動一動手會讓某些腦區活動起來，更多血液就會流向那裡。(E) 1970 年代中期的條目說 PET 呈現的是組織如何運作，而不是它的外觀（癌細胞消耗糖較快而亮起來）。其餘：(B) 唐納改造的是工廠用來找金屬裂縫的機器，不是一開始就為看胎兒設計的；(D) CT 仰賴 X 光，掃描太多次可能有害；(F) PET 用的糖本身就帶有微量放射性物質；(G) 1971 年的 CT 已經在第一位病人的腦中找到腫瘤，比 1990 年早得多；(H) 愛迪生的觀看器讓群眾看到自己的骨頭，他是因為助手 Dally 的遭遇大受震驚，才放棄 X 光研究。
evidence: Like many researchers of the day, he assumed his burns would heal with rest, but he lost both arms and died in 1904.
Because busy brain areas draw in extra oxygen-rich blood, scientists could watch the brain at work while a volunteer looked at flashing lights or moved a hand.
PET therefore shows how tissue is working rather than what it looks like.

option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯：1958 年的條目說唐納改造的是「工廠用來找金屬裂縫的機器」，看見子宮內的胎兒是後來的成果，不是原本的設計目的。
option_notes_zh.D: 與原文矛盾：1971 年的條目說 CT 仰賴 X 光，掃描太多次可能有害，並不是完全沒有輻射。
option_notes_zh.F: 只對一半：病人確實要先接受一種糖，但這種糖本身就帶有微量放射性物質（radioactive material），並沒有避開輻射。
option_notes_zh.G: 與時間軸矛盾：1971 年 CT 的第一位病人就被找到腦部腫瘤，早在 1990 年小川誠二的發現之前就能看到活人的大腦。
option_notes_zh.H: 原因錯：愛迪生的觀看器讓群眾排隊看自己的骨頭，並不是沒有用；他是因為助手 Dally 受到嚴重傷害（失去雙臂，後來過世）大受震驚，才放棄 X 光研究。

3.strategy_zh: 推論題：每個選項都要回到對應年份的條目找依據，再確認「推得出來」而不只是「沒提到」。正確的推論常藏在因果句裡（Like many researchers… he assumed…、Because busy brain areas…）；錯誤選項則常把細節換掉：機器原本的用途、糖帶不帶放射性、愛迪生放棄的原因、哪一年最早看到大腦。
hints: 每個選項先找出它說的是哪一年的方法，再回到那個條目核對。
Dally 以為灼傷會怎樣？這透露出當時的人對 X 光的了解有多少？
(F)(G)(H) 都用了原文的字，但「避開輻射」「第一個」「因為沒用」和原文一樣嗎？

A: Like many researchers of the day, he assumed his burns would heal with rest, but he lost both arms and died in 1904.
B: Working with an engineer, this Glasgow doctor adapted a machine that factories used to find cracks in metal.
C: Because busy brain areas draw in extra oxygen-rich blood, scientists could watch the brain at work while a volunteer looked at flashing lights or moved a hand.
D: CT has proved a double-edged sword, though: because it relies on X-rays, too many scans can be harmful.
E: PET therefore shows how tissue is working rather than what it looks like.
F: Before a PET scan, patients receive a form of sugar that carries a tiny amount of radioactive material.
G: Hounsfield’s scanner sent beams through the head from many angles while a computer turned the readings into thin slices, and in its first patient it revealed a brain tumor.
H: Edison built a viewer with a glowing screen, and crowds lined up to see their own bones.
Shocked, Edison gave up X-ray work.

4.explanation_zh: double-edged sword 字面是「兩邊都開了刃的劍」，比喻「有利也有弊的事物」，正是題幹 something that brings both benefits and risks 的意思。1971 年的條目說 CT 能看清一般 X 光照不清楚的大腦，但因為仰賴 X 光，掃描太多次可能有害，所以說 CT 是 a double-edged sword。題幹問名詞片語，答案寫 a double-edged sword（不寫 a、或不加連字號寫成 double edged 也可以），不要連 has proved 一起抄。
evidence: CT has proved a double-edged sword, though: because it relies on X-rays, too many scans can be harmful.
4.strategy_zh: 題幹用文中沒有的 benefits、risks 描述概念：先找哪一個條目同時說了某個方法的好處和壞處（CT 看得清大腦，但掃描太多次可能有害），再找那一句裡把這種情況說成一個名詞片語的地方，只寫片語本身。
hints: 哪一個條目同時提到某種方法的好處與壞處？
1971 年的條目在 though 前面把 CT 比喻成什麼？
答案是三個字的名詞片語，以 a double- 開頭。

translation_zh.text:
1895 年以前，醫生只能從身體外部判斷活人體內的狀況。下面的時間軸整理醫學影像的七個里程碑：每一項是誰做出來的、讓醫生看見了什麼，以及它不足的地方。

1895｜威廉‧倫琴
倫琴在德國測試一支玻璃管時，注意到一種看不見的射線，能輕易穿透皮肉，穿透骨頭卻困難得多。他拍下妻子的手，照片裡看得見她的骨頭和結婚戒指，讓大眾大為驚奇；短短幾個月內，醫生就開始用這種射線找出骨折的位置和體內的子彈。

1896｜湯瑪斯‧愛迪生
愛迪生做出一種裝有發光螢幕的觀看器，群眾排隊來看自己的骨頭。他的助手克萊倫斯‧達利一連好幾個小時把雙手放在射線管前面。和當時許多研究者一樣，他以為灼傷休息一陣子就會好，結果卻失去了雙臂，並在 1904 年過世。大受震驚的愛迪生從此放棄 X 光的研究。

1958｜伊恩‧唐納
這位格拉斯哥的醫生和一位工程師合作，改造了一台工廠用來找出金屬裂縫的機器。它把超音波，也就是人耳聽不見的高頻聲音，送進人體，再把回音轉成影像；他在 1958 年和同事發表的報告，收錄了第一批用這種方法拍到的子宮內胎兒影像。不過，骨頭和空氣會擋住聲波。

1971｜高佛雷‧豪斯菲爾德
一般的 X 光照片能把骨頭拍得很清楚，大腦卻看起來像一團霧。豪斯菲爾德的掃描機從許多角度讓射線穿過頭部，同時由電腦把讀數轉成一片片薄薄的切面；它在第一位病人身上就找到了腦部的腫瘤。不過，CT 也證明是一把雙面刃：因為它仰賴 X 光，掃描太多次可能有害。

1970 年代中期｜聖路易的一個團隊
做 PET 掃描之前，病人會先接受一種帶有微量放射性物質的糖。癌細胞消耗糖的速度比健康細胞快，所以會在螢幕上亮起來。因此，PET 呈現的是組織如何運作，而不是它的外觀。

1977｜雷蒙‧達馬迪安
他的團隊不用 X 光，而是用巨大的磁鐵和無線電波，做出了人體的第一張 MRI 影像：一張粗糙的胸部影像，花了將近五個小時才完成。今天的機器快得多，能把軟組織呈現得非常細緻，但病人必須完全靜止地躺著，因為任何移動都會讓影像變成一片模糊。

1990｜小川誠二
在美國工作的研究者小川誠二發現，MRI 能偵測血液攜帶了多少氧氣。由於正在活動的腦區會引進更多富含氧氣的血液，科學家便能在受試者看著閃爍的燈光或動一動手時，觀察大腦的運作。

Within months doctors used the rays to locate broken bones and bullets.
1896: Edison built a viewer with a glowing screen; crowds lined up to see their own bones.
Clarence Dally held his hands in front of the tubes for hours; like many researchers of the day he assumed his burns would heal with rest; he lost both arms and died in 1904.
Edison gave up X-ray work after what happened to Dally.
1958: Ian Donald, a Glasgow doctor, worked with an engineer to adapt a factory machine for finding cracks in metal.
Ultrasound is sound too high for human ears; echoes are turned into pictures.
Donald’s 1958 report with colleagues included the first ultrasound images of a baby in the womb.
Ordinary X-ray photographs show bones sharply but the brain looks like fog.
1971: Hounsfield’s CT scanner sent beams through the head from many angles and a computer turned the readings into slices; its first patient’s scan revealed a brain tumor.
CT relies on X-rays, so too many scans can be harmful.
Mid-1970s: a team in St. Louis (PET).
Before a PET scan patients receive a form of sugar carrying a tiny amount of radioactive material; cancer cells use sugar faster; PET shows how tissue works rather than what it looks like.
1977: Damadian’s team made the first MRI image of a human body, a rough chest picture that took nearly five hours.
MRI uses a huge magnet and radio waves instead of X-rays, shows soft tissue in fine detail; patients must lie still because movement blurs the picture; today’s machines are far quicker.
1990: Ogawa, a researcher in the United States, found MRI could detect how much oxygen the blood carries.
Busy brain areas draw in extra oxygen-rich blood, so scientists could watch the brain at work while a volunteer looked at flashing lights or moved a hand.
